[quote=astanir;60431387][b]Argossian Negotiations[/b]
With all the mainland tribes on the negotiating table, progress would finally start to make itself evident. News of the battles unfolding in the south and the east would motive the argossians to find a common ground, with the following being proposed to Nordiheim.
[list]
- The Argossian tribes of the mainland will unite their territories into a singular state, which will go by the name of "The tribal republic of Kuhaw-Astan"
- This state will act as a federation, allowing each tribe autonomy over a range of affairs and allowing each tribal leader a say in the government
- The military of this state will be split into units, with a unit being dedicated to a specific tribe. This will allow far more effective communication on the battle field and will allow each tribe to preserve their military traditions
- Nordiheim will provide this state with military equipment for the duration of the war and afterwards, unless the agreements made at this table are violated by either side
- Nordiheim will protect this state from unwanted external influence and harm, both military and economic, for the duration of the war and afterwards, unless the agreements made at this table are violated by either side
[/list]

Unaware of the enemy they were facing, the sui-mana would use the Nordiheimian equipment to continue their push against the Democrats, however they would not make much progress and eventually the democrats would begin to push them back. After several calls from Nordiheim, the Sui-mana leadership would eventually stand down and withdraw, focusing their forces against the nationalists in the south.

When questioned about communication with the cheiftains, the tribes would come up blank. No communications had been made since they were notified of their arrival in teremok, which has prompted great suspicion about the councils.

[b]The stronghold island[/b]
After the Nordiheimians had been surveying off the coast of the stronghold island for the past fews days, The Restorationists would launch their naval task force to confront Nordiheim, consisting of the following:
[list]
- 1 submarine
- 5 frigates
- 3 destroyers
-2 cruisers

They would fire upon Nordiheim as soon as they came into view.
[/list]

[b]The lower islands[/b]
The antiair defences would be set up as quickly as possible and targeted at the incoming F-15s and their payloads. Apart from this, the argossians would not have any other counters to the F-15s, nor any of the incoming missiles. In the sea, the argossian's own ships would be quickly worn down by the join forces of the UDF and the PDF's airborn bombardments.

The main defence would have to be left to the Nordiheimians, whilst the Argossians would retire to the island and begin to engage in guerilla tactics, which would most likely allow the UDF to make a landing. The guerilla tactics would at first be dealt with by the UDF by rallying into central positions, but argossian snipers would easily be able to pick them off like this by hiding in the tall, untouched grasses of the islands. Once the numbers of the large gatherings had been reduced, the main forces would move in to surround them, easily outnumbering them at this point.

(tbh not much for me to say here, from this point onwards Nordiheimian forces will be doing most of the air and naval fighting.)

[b]Change of Leadership in the restoration front[/b]
after months of disjointed fighting, a new set of leaders have finally risen up in the armed restoration front to fill the vacant seats of the military council. Thew new council members are:
[list]
- General Akuini
- General Saloa
- General Loni
[/list]

The primitive air defences of the Argos proved to be obsolete in countering the F-15's assualt. Once a AA system locked onto an F-15, they'd sharply turn back to create as much distance between the two, when the AA launched its missiles the F-15s would scramble away wearing out the missiles system until it eventually caught up, where they'd then preform an evasive manoeuvre barreling down towards the sea where'd the radar of the missile spoofed and it lost its course. Only one F-15 was succesfully hit, but even so, it was due to a preterm detonation giving the aircraft survivable wounds. 

On the ground, it was another story. UDF forces overwhelemed and overpowered Argossian central military combatants. But with this crushing defeat rose an unconventional assymetrical style of warfare which perfectly countered the UDF's positions. Snipers took out scrambling UDF forces making capturing the islands successfully a logistical nightmare. To combat this, the UDF dispatched drones to survey designated "sniper zones" where a marked sniper was believed to be located. Once a sniper was found or evidence leaned towards their potential whereabouts, loitering muntions were silently dispatched. Hunting for these snipers feets above the surface of the dense Argossian jungles. 

Though for larger guerilla forces, the volume of firepower used to neutralize them was on a different level. When hostile guerilla forces were marked on an estimated location, F-111 Aardvarks and F-117 Nighthawks were dispatched towards their locations, where they'd deploy napalm and clustering munitions in the general area of the marked zone. This was the UDF's more efficient way of combating the guerilla forces. 

But that wasn't it. Deep behind the frontlines, heavy battery systems hid under the dense forest canopy. Camoflauged and hidden, these batteries were specialized for deep battle survival. They'd relay information back and forth between forces fighting in the frontlines, data such as wind resistance, locations, horizon depth, etc were all needed to operate these conventional batteries. Once sufficient information was gathered, the batteries were armed and they let forth their hellfire in the form of salvoing. But these shells weren't any normal shells, knowing that direct hits on decentralized guerilla forces would be almost impossible with conventional munitions, the UDF decided to instead use poison gas infused canisters that spread all across the north of the islands. UDF forces fighting within the frontlines were suited with protective gas masks to ensure no friendly fire took place. The gas diffused all throughout the islands north, deep in guerilla territory. Only obeying the direction of the wind, the gas layed all hell on the Argossians. Suffocating and killing its unsuspecting victims before they could even  yell for help. Now the UDF waited to advance. They took this time lick their wounds and reroute logistical routes, and for a 2 day period, the steam of the UDF halted.
